title: Every leopard has its own rosettes
storyboard: Film: our camera-trap clip of a leopard passing on a forest trail (IR night or dawn), 10–15 s

scenes.headline: Rosettes are a leopard's ID card
scenes.body: Researchers match spot patterns to tell individual leopards apart in camera-trap photos.

scenes.headline: One leopard, matched across 8 years
scenes.body: Bandipur, Karnataka: a 2012 photo matched a 2004 camera-trap image by its rosettes.

scenes.label: leopards estimated in India (2022)
scenes.body: Counted with camera traps at 32,803 locations.

caption:
Our camera trap doesn't just see a leopard. It sees which leopard.

Karnataka's 2022 estimate was 1,879 leopards, the third-highest of any state.

Source: WII/NTCA 'Status of Leopards in India 2022'; WCS (2012). Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Storyboard: the CC clips stand in for our own camera-trap footage. Trail-cam is our highest-reach original format; this one turns the clip into a lesson on photo-ID science.
